questions.title: The circulation with two sequential capillary beds
questions.question: The specific circulatory pathway that is well known to contain exactly two sequential capillary beds is the circulation located between which organs?

options.A: The completely entire circulation located between the heart and the kidneys
options.B: The entirely complete systemic circulation between the heart and the external skin
options.C: The completely separate pulmonary circulation between the active lungs and the heart

explanations.A: Incorrect. Blood flows from the heart to the kidneys and back through a single renal capillary bed (the glomerulus and peritubular capillaries in series counts as one functional organ circuit), not two beds separated by a portal vein without an intervening pass through the heart.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The systemic circulation to the skin is a single capillary bed returning directly to the heart, the ordinary pattern, not the two-bed exception this question tests.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The pulmonary circulation is a single capillary bed sitting between two chambers of the heart (right ventricle to left atrium) — a different arrangement from two beds in series with no pass through the heart between them.
explanations.D: Correct. Blood leaves capillary beds in the stomach, intestines, pancreas and spleen, collects into the portal vein, and passes through a second capillary-like bed — the hepatic sinusoids — inside the liver before finally draining into the hepatic veins and the systemic circulation. This is the hepatic portal circulation: two capillary beds in series, with no pass through the heart in between, letting the liver process absorbed nutrients before they reach general circulation.

questions.learning_objective: Name the hepatic portal circulation as the pathway with two sequential capillary beds.
